nodes.summary: Alice walks down a list of candidates, announcing for each whether it is her input; the protocol continues with `k a` for the revealed candidate `a`, and inputs not in the list end at the output `false`.
nodes.title: Alice reveals her input from a list

nodes.summary: Alice announces the `b` bits of the message `v x`, one at a time, and the protocol then continues with `k m` for the announced message `m`.
nodes.title: Alice sends a `b`-bit message

nodes.summary: The analogue of `aliceReveal` for Bob.
nodes.title: Bob reveals his input from a list

nodes.summary: If `f` has a fooling set `S`, then `|S| ≤ 2 ^ D(f)`, that is `D(f) ≥ log₂ |S|` (S. Arora and B. Barak, *Computational Complexity*, web draft of 2007-01-08, Lemma 12.4).
nodes.title: Fooling-set lower bound for `D(f)`

nodes.summary: If `f` has a fooling set `S`, every protocol computing `f` has depth `d` with `|S| ≤ 2 ^ d` (S. Arora and B. Barak, *Computational Complexity*, web draft of 2007-01-08, Lemma 12.4).
nodes.title: Fooling-set lower bound

nodes.summary: A protocol of depth `d` has at most `2 ^ d` leaves (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Lemma 1.2).
nodes.title: A protocol of depth `d` has at most `2 ^ d` leaves

nodes.summary: For zero-bit strings equality is the constant `true`, computed with no communication, so its communication complexity is `0`.
nodes.title: Equality of empty strings

nodes.summary: For `n ≥ 1`, equality of `n`-bit strings has deterministic communication complexity exactly `n + 1` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Theorem 1.14, with the trivial protocol for the upper bound). For `n = 0` the function is constant and the complexity is `0`.
nodes.title: Deterministic communication complexity of equality

nodes.summary: Every protocol computing `f` has depth at least `commComplexity f`.
nodes.title: Every protocol costs at least `D(f)`

nodes.summary: `commComplexity f` is the least depth of a protocol computing `f : X → Y → Bool` (A. C. Yao, STOC 1979; A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 1). For finite inputs such a protocol always exists (`Protocol.exists_computes`). If no protocol computes `f`, which is possible only for infinite inputs, the value is `0` by the convention `sInf ∅ = 0`.
nodes.title: Deterministic communication complexity

nodes.summary: The matrix of `f : X → Y → Bool` over a ring `K`, with entry `1` at `(x, y)` when `f x y` holds and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Communication matrix

nodes.summary: `p.Computes f` when the output of `p` on every input pair `(x, y)` is `f x y`.
nodes.title: A protocol computes a function

nodes.summary: If every continuation costs at most `d` bits, then `aliceSends b v k` costs at most `b + d` bits.
nodes.title: Cost of sending a `b`-bit message

nodes.summary: The trivial protocol costs at most `n + 1` bits (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 1: "Alice can send Bob her input, and Bob can respond with the value of a function, giving a protocol with communication `n + 1`").
nodes.title: Upper bound for equality

nodes.summary: The depth of its tree: the largest number of bits exchanged on any input.
nodes.title: Communication cost of a protocol

nodes.summary: `eqFn n x y` holds exactly when the `n`-bit strings `x` and `y` are equal.
nodes.title: Equality function

nodes.summary: If a protocol computes `f`, then `f` takes the same value on any two input pairs that reach the same leaf, and on the crossed pair (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Theorem 1.7).
nodes.title: Leaf rectangles are monochromatic

nodes.summary: The trivial protocol computes equality.
nodes.title: The trivial protocol computes equality

nodes.summary: Alice sends her `n` bits and Bob announces whether they equal his input: `n + 1` bits.
nodes.title: The trivial protocol for equality

nodes.summary: If `x` is in the candidate list, the run of `aliceReveal l k` on `(x, y)` ends as the run of `k x` does.
nodes.title: Alice reveals her input

nodes.summary: The run of `aliceSends b v k` on `(x, y)` ends as the run of `k (v x)` does.
nodes.title: Output after Alice sends a message

nodes.summary: If `y` is in the candidate list, the run of `bobReveal l k` on `(x, y)` ends as the run of `k y` does.
nodes.title: Bob reveals his input

nodes.summary: Two runs with the same transcript end at the same leaf, so they produce the same output.
nodes.title: The output is determined by the transcript

nodes.summary: The label of the leaf reached when Alice holds `x` and Bob holds `y`.
nodes.title: Output of a protocol

nodes.summary: Alice reveals `x`, then Bob reveals `y`, and the leaf reached is labelled `f x y`.
nodes.title: Every function on finite inputs has a protocol

nodes.summary: For finite inputs, some protocol computing `f` has depth exactly `commComplexity f`.
nodes.title: An optimal protocol exists

nodes.summary: If a protocol computes `f`, distinct pairs of a fooling set for `f` have distinct transcripts (S. Arora and B. Barak, *Computational Complexity*, web draft of 2007-01-08, proof of Lemma 12.4).
nodes.title: Fooling-set pairs reach distinct leaves

nodes.summary: A finite set `S` of input pairs is a fooling set for `f` with value `b` when `f = b` on `S` and, for any two distinct pairs `(x₁, y₁)` and `(x₂, y₂)` of `S`, either `f x₁ y₂ ≠ b` or `f x₂ y₁ ≠ b` (S. Arora and B. Barak, *Computational Complexity*, web draft of 2007-01-08, Definition 12.3).
nodes.title: Fooling set

nodes.summary: The set of root-to-leaf paths, each written as the list of bits announced along it.
nodes.title: Leaves of a protocol tree

nodes.summary: There is a constant `C` such that every Boolean function `f` on finite inputs has deterministic communication complexity at most `C (log₂ rank M_f + 1) ^ C`, the rank taken over `ℝ` (L. Lovász and M. Saks, 1988; stated as Conjecture 2.12 in A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, as `D(M) ≤ log^α rank(M)`). The additive `+ 1` and the factor `C` make the statement meaningful for matrices…
nodes.title: The log-rank conjecture (open)

nodes.summary: Over any field `K`, `⌈log₂ rank M_f⌉ ≤ D(f)`; since `D(f)` is an integer, this is `log₂ rank M_f ≤ D(f)` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Theorem 2.11: "If a matrix has rank `r`, then its communication complexity is at least `log r`").
nodes.title: Log-rank lower bound

nodes.summary: For `n ≥ 1`, every protocol computing equality of `n`-bit strings has depth at least `n + 1`: the `2 ^ n` diagonal pairs reach distinct leaves with output `1`, and some other leaf has output `0` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Claim 1.13 and Theorem 1.14).
nodes.title: Lower bound for equality

nodes.summary: A protocol for inputs `x : X` (held by Alice) and `y : Y` (held by Bob) is a binary tree: a leaf `output b` announces the Boolean `b`; a node `alice f p₀ p₁` has Alice announce the bit `f x` and continue with `p₀` or `p₁` accordingly; a node `bob g p₀ p₁` has Bob announce `g y` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Chapter 1, "Defining 2 party protocols"; A. C. Yao, STOC 1979).
nodes.title: Deterministic two-party protocol

nodes.summary: Over any field `K`, `rank M_f ≤ 2 ^ D(f)` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Lemma 2.10 with Theorem 1.7).
nodes.title: Rank lower bound for `D(f)`

nodes.summary: Over any field `K`, if a protocol of depth `d` computes `f`, then the communication matrix of `f` has rank at most `2 ^ d`; equivalently `d ≥ log₂ rank M_f` (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Lemma 2.10 and Theorem 2.11; S. Arora and B. Barak, *Computational Complexity*, web draft of 2007-01-08, Theorem 12.10 `χ(f) ≥ rank M(f)` with Theorem 12.7 `C(f) ≥ log₂ χ(f)`).
nodes.title: Rank lower bound

nodes.summary: If the runs on `(x, y)` and `(x', y')` have the same transcript, then so does the run on the crossed pair `(x, y')`.
nodes.title: Crossing property of transcripts

nodes.summary: The inputs on which a protocol follows a given path `π` form a combinatorial rectangle `A × B`, with `A` the inputs of Alice that reach `π` against some input of Bob and `B` symmetrically (A. Rao and A. Yehudayoff, *Communication Complexity*, early draft, Lemmas 1.5 and 1.6).
nodes.title: Rectangle lemma

nodes.summary: The transcript of every run is the path of a leaf of the protocol tree.
nodes.title: Transcripts are leaf paths

nodes.summary: The list of bits announced on inputs `(x, y)`; it names the root-to-leaf path the run follows.
nodes.title: Transcript of a protocol

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
